newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Sydney airport choice in 1997 - Australia govt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Sydney airport choice in 1997 - Australia govt.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said on Wednesday he expected to make a decision about the site of Sydney's second airport by the end of 1997.

"By the end of the third quarter next year, we certainly expect to be equipped with the relevant information to enable us to make a decision," Sharp told reporters. "We'll be in a position to make a decision by the end of next year."
Sharp said once the government had chosen either Badgerys Creek or Holsworthy as the second airport site, construction of the airport would then take about four years to complete.
Construction of the airport would take place in stages, he said.
The second airport was originally planned to open in time for the expected flood of foreign arrivals for the 2000 Olympic Games in Sydney.
Sharp also said Badgerys Creek was still the government's preferred site.
"Badgery's Creek still remains our preferred site for a second Sydney airport and I think it's important for us to state that in an event like this," he said.
Sydney's existing airport at Mascot is Australia's busiest domestic and international gateway, but is restricted by a night curfew and a limit of 80 flight movements each hour.
